sentences.text: Musturzabalsuchus is an extinct genus containing only one species of allodaposuchid eusuchian crocodyliform.
The genus name Musturzabalsuchus means "broadened rostrum crocodile", combining the Basque word for broadened rostrum and the Greek word for crocodile.
The first material assigned to Musturzabalsuchus was found in 1997 at the locality of Laño in northern Spain.
Despite many remains being found, the only known skeletal elements of Musturzabalsuchus are the maxilla and mandible.
A specimen from the Fuvelian Lignites in France was referred to Musturzabalsuchus in 1999.
Later research challenged the specific traits used to link that French fossil to this genus.
Material from Valencia, Spain, dates to the Early or Middle Campanian, making it slightly older than specimens from other localities.
Recent phylogenetic studies classify Musturzabalsuchus as a member of the family Allodaposuchidae, outside the group Alligatoroidea.
Musturzabalsuchus is often omitted from phylogenetic analyses because of insufficient anatomical information.
A 2015 phylogenetic analysis found that Musturzabalsuchus is a member of the family Allodaposuchidae, evolutionarily distant from Alligatoroidea.
Musturzabalsuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically either the Late Campanian or very Early Maastrichtian stages.
Musturzabalsuchus was endemic to Europe and likely restricted to the Ibero-Armorica Island, as it is absent from Northern and Eastern European localities.
Musturzabalsuchus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, approximately 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
